newsitem.title: BELGIUM: SOCCER SHOWCASE-PEN PICTURES OF EKEREN PLAYERS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-PEN PICTURES OF EKEREN PLAYERS.

text.p: Pen pictures of the players most likely to play for Ekeren against Anderlecht in the Belgian Cup final on Sunday:

Philippe Vande Walle, goalkeeper, 35. Dynamic and spectacular, automatic choice for national team but is now back-up for Sporting Lisbon's Filip De Wilde. Regularly converts penalties and has occasionally rushed forward in dying minutes to score and -- successfully -- save his team from defeat. Excellent physique and reflexes, lithe and rarely injured with nearly 400 matches under his belt at Ekeren.
Matthew Andrews, goalkeeper, 26. British understudy to Vande Walle for the past seven years but rarely given the occasion to make a name for himself.
Didier Dheedene, defender, 25. Reliable left-back with quick mind, mainstay in defence but drafted by Anderlecht from next season which already seen as team's biggest loss.
Mike Verstraeten, defender, 29. Lanky and solid central defender, commanding in the air.
Marc Schaessens, defender, 28. Fast and tenacious right-back with offensive drive who easily creates openings down his wing.
Bernard Wegria, defender, 34. Solid defender with good physique but has waned in second half of season and expected to leave.
Rudy Janssens, defender, 33. Has earned a regular berth with no-nonsense defensive play and good positional sense.
Christophe Kinet, midfielder, 22. Technically strong and maturing fast, one of the team's brightest prospects. Known for lightning-fast runs down the wings.

Florian Urban, midfielder, 28. Hard-tackling, uncompromising and hot-tempered Hungarian, often in trouble at former clubs where he was always in the front line during tussles. Has almost learned to control his quick temper. Strong utility player, good at creating openings.
Cvejan Milosevic, midfielder, 33. The team's main force in midfield but absent in recent weeks due to groin injury. Bosnian but former Yugoslav international.
Gunther Hofmans, midfielder, 30. Former striker who has turned into skilful support player while retaining his goalscoring touch although very erratic this season. Son-in-law of club chairman.

Alex Czerniatynski, striker, 36. Former Belgian international whose age is gradually showing. Limited technical abilities largely compensated by immense fighting spirit and often drafted as super-sub at crucial times.

Tomasz Radzinski, striker, 23. The team's most potent weapon, Very fast, scored a hat-trick in league game against Anderlecht earlier this month and again in last match on Sunday. Battled his way to fitness after first half of season was spoiled by injuries and call-ups for Canadian national team. Not always stylish but devastating shot and real match-winner.

Edwin Van Ankeren, striker, 28. Former Dutch international who has been plagued by injuries this season and played mostly below par but has improved in recent weeks and may have found his goal-scoring touch just in time.
